newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Berisha blames communists, foreigners for riots.
newsitem.headline: Berisha blames communists, foreigners for riots.

text.p: Albanian President Sali Berisha accused ex-communists and foreign spies on Sunday of stoking civil unrest and vowed to use the "iron hand" of the law to quash violent protests against his right-wing government.
In a televised address, Berisha blamed foreign intelligence agencies and the former communist elite for a bloody uprising in the south of the country that claimed up to nine lives over the weekend.

"Armed communist rebels, helped and financed by foreign espionage services, have started military actions to overthrow the government by force and establish their rule across the country," Berisha said.
"Constitutional law and order has been violated and so have...the institutions and the territorial integrity of Albania, creating conditions to engulf Albania in a civil war."

Berisha was speaking after parliament, dominated by his Democratic Party, voted unanimously to declare a state of emergency. The assembly was responding to two months of rioting sparked by the collapse of popular pyramid investment schemes.

"I pledge that every means envisaged by law will be used to crush the red terrorist rebellion and that we will react with the greatest toughness against all those who are desecrating Albania and its democracy," Berisha said, without elaborating.
"They will very soon feel the iron hand and the full punishment of the laws of this state."
The president called on Albanians to defend democracy and warned against a return to the Stalinist rule that isolated Albania from its neighbours for half a century.

"Let us not forget that the communist dictatorship was our greatest plight. Democracy belongs to all political forces that respect it. Let us defend it from the red violence, from the terrorrists and rebels that have no principles," Berisha said.
"Terrorists" and "red bandits" had already taken control of parts of southern Albania, he said.
In the Adriatic town of Sarande, rioters looted police headquarters then cruised the streets shooting into the air with Kalashnikov assault rifles.
The southern port of Vlore was scene of the worst violence over the weekend, with up to nine people killed in a shoot-out between secret police and angry pyramid investors.
Berisha also appealed to the international community to show solidarity with Albania.
"I appeal to the civilised world, friendly countries in Europe and the world to express their solidarity in defence of Albanian democracy," he said.
